chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Meeting Django at the Brasserie Alsacienne
summary: Noel Chiboust introduced Briggs to Django in a Rue Fontaine cafe; Django, living in his caravan, was unconcerned about work but agreed to join Briggs's proposition.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, how did you come across Django in the first place?

I met Django -- there was a cafe on the Rue Fontaine, which was called La Brasserie Alsacienne. C'est existe toujours. It doesn't exist anymore. It was transformed into something else. But it was right next to the Chountine Cabaret, and it was what you would call a meeting place that most musicians after work, we'd go and have a supper or something. And that's where we met -- I would think he was not with Vola. He was with Noel Chiboust -- you ever heard of him?
Yeh, sure.
He was with Noel Chiboust at the table, with Noel Chiboust, when I walked into the place. Chiboust called me over, 'cause I knew Chiboust, he was second
Briggs 307
trumpet in the band that played Salle de Pleyel.
Yes.
Coleman Hawkins --
He was a hot trumpet player?
Yes, yes. Didn't have much lips. Wonderful ideas, but not much lips.
And he introduced me to Django. He said, (unintelligible) Django." "Oh, my brother, I've heard of you so long / and, "I'm glad to meet you and everything."
I told him, I said, "Now," he said, "What're you doing?" I said, "Well, "I'm working in different places."
And he said, -- well, at the time the Music Box was open. It's not that Music Box, but another Music Box on Rue Pigalle, right opposite the Le Gran Duc. It was called "The Music Box".
And he said, (unintelligible) "I go
Briggs 308
to the Music Box, I have a good time, so I play."
I said, "But are you working someplace?" He said, "No". He said, "Working; I don't worry about working." (Laughter). It was just one of those things. He said, "I got my --". What do you call it--
Like a little camping trailer.
Yeh, yeh. And he said, "As long as I have my cabin, no worries, I can always get something to eat." "Oh, my brother, I know you'll give me something to eat." (Laughter).

Well, we had gotten together, and I told him about the proposition that I had, and it interested him. We came together. I understood that Saturday night, when we had the best crowd take over, it didn't make no difference if he was there or he isn't there, one of his brothers
Briggs
I see.
